source_review.notes: Checked POSA2 Proactor foundations; current Microsoft I/O completion port and asynchronous I/O documentation; current Linux io_uring/io_uring_enter documentation; current Boost.Asio and libuv documentation; RFC 9293; and the cited network, systems and performance texts. Backend-specific submission, completion, buffer, cancellation and close claims are scoped and dated.

evidence: Checked operation lifecycle, terminal result set, buffer lease, owner generation, rate/duration/outstanding-work and SQ/CQ notation.
Confirmed Little's Law units and terminal/cancellation state distinctions are consistent.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Operation acceptance, primitive progress, terminal completion, handler return and durable business effect remain separate.

evidence: Recomputed Exercise 2: 20,000 operations/s times 0.004 s = 80 average outstanding operations.
Recomputed 80 times 16 KiB = 1,280 KiB = 1.25 MiB average buffers.
Reproduced two submissions, two cancel requests, out-of-order success/cancel results, cancel-lost flag, duplicate suppression, two terminal records and post-terminal buffer release.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No real device/runtime latency, SQ/CQ behavior, registered memory, handler tails, cancellation distribution or backend workload was measured.

evidence: Verified atomic nonterminal-to-result transition admits at most one logical terminal handler per stable operation identity.
Confirmed exclusive buffer lease from pre-submission through actual terminal reaping prevents conflicting reuse through the modeled path.
Derived N=lambda*W as a stable-average accounting relationship and checked why it does not bound tails.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Local terminal uniqueness does not prove one I/O execution or one external business effect; unsafe pointers/platform defects and liveness remain outside the arguments.

evidence: Reviewed immediate rejection, inline/pending completion, short/zero/EOF/error results, composed-step limits, out-of-order/duplicate completions and sequence-dependent writes.

evidence: Traced stable operation context, normalized initiation, buffer lifetime, result precision, out-of-order handling, cancel/timeout reaping, bounded outstanding work, bounded handlers, serialization and safe shutdown through exposition/examples/answers.

evidence: Reviewed terminal uniqueness argument from stable identity and atomic terminal cell.
Reviewed buffer-lifetime argument from exclusive lease until documented terminal ownership return.

evidence: Audited asynchronous, accepted, completed, cancelled, exactly once, safe, valid, ordered, atomic, durable, proof, every and conclusion language.
